svg.text: A funnel of failed pseudoscience examples narrows into Feynman's central diagnosis—missing scientific
integrity—which then fans out into principles and is tested against a chain of real-world case studies.

g.text: The talk funnels several failed investigations into one diagnosis (missing integrity), spells out that integrity as
satellite principles, then walks through case studies that test it before closing.

g.title: Why people still believe nonsense — Science arose by testing and discarding failed ideas, yet mysticism and pseudoscience persist. — → spya-ddrr9m

"Cargo Cult Science": the form of research without real results — Islanders mimic airstrips and control towers, but no planes land — the missing ingredient is scientific integrity. — → spya-fd2muf
Report everything that could make your result wrong — → spya-afgs74

g.text: CASE STUDIES PUT TO THE TEST
A funnel: several independent failed searches for substance, all leading nowhere, set up the need for a diagnosis.

g.text: A hub: the cargo cult diagnosis opens into several concrete demands integrity places on scientists, tested against the
